Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient-stimulus ATAC/CUT&RUN time course with washout
ideas.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) to a brief stimulus that induces FOS/JUN, then wash out and profile AP-1 binding (CUT&RUN) and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) over days to weeks. Persistent AP-1-dependent accessible regions after FOS/JUN levels return to baseline (like 'unclothe'-ing chromatin that stays open) would indicate memory. Compare to naive cells.

ideas.title: Acute degron depletion at different phases (induction vs maintenance)
ideas.description: Use dTAG/AID degrons on FOS, JUN or other AP-1 members and remove AP-1 either during stimulation or only after the stimulus ended. If memory requires AP-1 only for establishing but not maintaining accessibility, versus continuous AP-1 for maintenance, the two phases are separated. Read out chromatin state and faster secondary-challenge transcription.

ideas.title: Secondary-challenge priming assay with AP-1 motif perturbation
ideas.description: Give two stimulus pulses separated by a rest interval and measure transcriptional response (RNA-seq, nascent PRO-seq) of primed versus naive cells. Use CRISPR mutation or dCas9-KRAB repression of specific AP-1 motifs at candidate enhancers to test whether those sites are necessary for the enhanced second response.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome lineage tracking of AP-1 history
ideas.description: Combine single-cell RNA plus ATAC with a fluorescent AP-1 reporter or barcoded lineage tracing to link past AP-1 activity to current chromatin state across cell divisions. Test whether daughter cells inherit the accessibility and responsiveness of mothers, and whether inheritance depends on AP-1 dosage, quantifying heritability versus noise.

ideas.title: Live-cell imaging and mathematical modeling of AP-1 dynamics
ideas.description: Track AP-1 activity with live reporters and single-molecule imaging of FOS/JUN residence times in stimulation-washout experiments, then fit models to test for bistability or hysteresis (self-sustaining state) versus passive decay. Predictions such as dose-dependent persistence thresholds can be tested by titrating the stimulus and by perturbing feedback loops (e.g., JUN autoregulation).
